newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE COCOA UP ON TRADE BUYING IN THIN VOLUME.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE COCOA UP ON TRADE BUYING IN THIN VOLUME.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa ended higher after jumping in afternoon business on trade buying, traders said.
"Basically, there's a little bit of trade buying coming in," one trader said.
Low volume made the market vulnerable to be pushed either way by a small volume of business, he said. "I think the market's going to come down, because there's no interest."
By the close September was ten stg higher at 1,011 stg, with 773 lots done. Active December was nine stg higher at 1,041 stg, on volume of 1,087 of the total 2,838 lots.
Sterling's fall might normally have been expected to make cocoa come up, but its effect had been offset by a weak New York, he said.
The Bank of England raised official interest rates on Thursday for the fourth month in a row and sent the pound tumbling by hinting that this would be the last policy tightening for some time.
Europe's cash cocoa trade has been languishing in summer doldrums this week, but sterling's dip from recent peaks has prompted some industry offtake, traders said on Thursday.
